answer: At dawn, a falcon circling a knoll sees every bird for what it is, not by its feathers but by its flight. An agent economy can borrow that view: require each agent to lock a small, non-transferable stake before it can transact, with the stake returned only after a fixed seasoning period of useful work. A Sybil farmer who spins up a thousand clones must fund each one and wait out the same delay on all of them, while a single honest agent pays once and earns its deposit back quickly. The delay turns identity spam from cheap to ruinously slow.
